tx_load_numerics.scope: Selected package and differential-input coupling. Fixed 1us, 7mA release waveform, 50ns voltage-envelope rise, hard or 20ns voltage-envelope fall, squared envelope current; same source samples across grids. Current solver retains assigned 200ps pole. Compare only active 1us interval. Grid and guard changes isolated. Finest FFT is a numerical comparator, not an exact transient; this isolates a mechanism and does not replace full-packet refinement or characterize silicon.

sinusoidal_controls.scope: Known sinusoidal current fundamental through the same continuous-frequency network and 200ps pole, compared with resampled FFT output at steady central samples. Tests representation, not the independently tested network itself. Source-hold images and finite switching transients are not part of the exact fundamental. A tone above grid Nyquist aliases; conserved integrated charge cannot preserve its frequency-dependent impedance or timing effect.

native_continuation.scope: Native incremental load-state serialization, quiet-gap decay and second activity window compared to one uninterrupted trace. First response extrapolates a 2us quiet tail but commits state only at the supplied input end. Zero incremental quiet current is an explicit warm-bias assumption. Not joined RX/TX or RF/wired protocol lifecycle qualification.

filter_realization.definition: Replace each normalized ideal integrator 1/z by 1/[z*(1+z/rho)], hence H(z) becomes H(z+z*z/rho). Retuning maps intended prototype zeros and poles to p+p*p/rho_nominal before the actual substitution; weights are unconstrained. Stability threshold is max(Im(p)^2/-Re(p)); equality has a marginal imaginary-axis pole.
filter_realization.scope: Explicit linear realization surrogate, not a transistor topology or universal op-amp GBW law. Same selected package/timing/internal/ADC activity and causal SAR/recharge wideband diagnostic. Wanted -65 dBm, blocker -30 dBm at +12 MHz, fixed 42 dB PGA, assigned NF/IIP3 and ideal DATA framing/training; not a standards-valid packet or PER. Retune requires realizable coefficients and characterization; +/-10% actual pole drift keeps nominal coefficients. No extra amplifier noise, slew/internal saturation, finite DC gain, mismatch or additional poles. Bias scenarios assume ten independent gm/C stages and gm/Id; exclude compensation, mirrors, output stages, references and other RF support. They are conditional cost requirements, not GF180 predictions or a 16 mA fit claim.

operating_conditions.scope: Temperature affects frontend and sampling thermal noise only; gain, delay, phase noise, leakage and current temperature coefficients are not modeled.

owner_reconciliation.scope: Current architecture block allocations summed by their assigned supply, including the separate CONV branch. Selected source override applied once; no overlap refund or converter-current reattribution. These are planning ceilings, not measured demand, individual bond limits or transient supply qualification.

rc_noise_and_capacitive_drive.scope: Joint optimization for the first (-65/-30 dBm) tone stimulus only, subject to the same passband/integrated noise targets. Explicit active summing resistors add thermal noise; integrator-input amplifier noise retains the existing illustrative gamma/gm law. Separate input and class-A output banks reserve peak capacitive current, not a universal minimum or class-AB average. A convex dual bound checks numerical cost rejection within that model. Integration plate areas use existing 0.9/1.8 fF/um2 density scenarios, without routing/guard/tuning overhead or guaranteed provider availability; all other RF area must remain inside the 2.4 mm2 owner. Actual resistor-driver implementation, amplifier voltage-noise gain, compensation/loop stability with Cint, summer noise/current and physical common mode remain unpriced. Stronger-tone demands reuse these same capacitors.
rc_noise_and_capacitive_drive.resistor_drive_scope: Conservative sum of independent branch peak currents into ideal virtual-ground summers, using existing sizes and the first tone stimulus. Separate class-A reservation, not measured consumption or a necessary minimum: shared drivers, phase cancellation and class-AB operation can change cost. Does not include numerator summer implementation or finite virtual-ground errors. No reoptimization.

filter_budget.basis: Unity-DC real pole plus two LP/BP state-variable notch sections; permutations are design-time alternatives, not new routing controls. Integrator noise sources are independent real one-sided voltage densities. ENBW=rate*C*P*C.T/2 with A*P+P*A.T=-B*B.T. Total NF=6 dB is partitioned between a 3/5 dB frontend and filter, rather than counted twice. Noise gain and node headroom use the existing 2.5 V floor; tone excitation separately uses the 3.6 V model ceiling to avoid cancelling stored high-gain excitation against low-rail headroom. This is a separated-rail screen, not a simulated rail transition. Illustrative e_n^2=4*k*T*gamma/gm and gm>=2*pi*fp*C_min; minimum summed gm satisfies the integrated and 401 sampled passband noise constraints. Required C=gm/(2*pi*fp) increases when noise forces higher gm, keeping the shared-bandwidth hypothesis consistent. Currents include two I/Q copies.
filter_budget.scope: Voltage-scaled linear mathematical candidate, not transistor design. Outer noise_bandwidth_bias fields are amplifier-drive-noise-only comparisons. Nested rc_noise_and_capacitive_drive adds explicit summing-resistor noise, integration capacitors and a separate class-A capacitive-drive hypothesis. Mirrors, actual resistor-driver implementation, complete amplifier voltage-noise gain, excess/flicker noise, finite DC gain, common mode, nonlinear internal swing and additional poles remain absent. Uniform effective bandwidth and ideal coefficient retuning. Sampled NF lacks an inter-frequency enclosure and does not establish complete receiver NF, EVM or sensitivity. Required compensation capacitance is an unpriced implementation obligation. Sampled steady-tone node peaks omit OFDM crest factor, switching histories and feedback of saturation. Paired RX-filter costs are compared with their current block allocation, excluding budgets owned by other RF blocks. Exceeding it rejects that scenario; a smaller cost does not prove physical fit.

finite_host_edge_network.scope: Fixed former 1 nF comparison network, not a selected reservoir. Host-only AC forcing: D2H mean-data and alternating H2D, split bank supply and separate external return; charge/DC unchanged. 100 ps kernel half-width is an assigned source hypothesis with 200 ps support, not a measured GPIO edge. No ADC/core/timing/reference switching, input clock, arbitrary phase, device feedback, DC rail-domain validity or rigorous infinite-tail bound. High-frequency lumped extrapolation diagnoses numerical convergence, not physical accuracy.

host_input_library_evidence.energy_unit_basis: Internal-power table energy scale V_unit^2*C_unit = pJ. Do not use leakage_power_unit or current_unit as the dynamic-energy scale. Preserve 7 pC as an adverse unvalidated scenario, not a measured receiver value.

converter.diagnostic_scope: Ratiometric internal endpoint with optional effective source charge per quarter-reference lane, lumped at acquisition end. Same finite acquisition and retained reference/DAC/comparator path. Zero effective capacitance is an ideal-load control. Continuous source impedance/bias, ratio mismatch and switch injection remain unmodeled. Cannot establish absolute VREF or independent gain accuracy.
converter.timing_ownership: Acquisition timestamps supplied by sample clock; allocated local completion intervals need no further external LO edges. Not a physical sequencer implementation.
converter.scope: Predictive conditional charge/settling/decision recurrence, not fitted silicon. Effective CDAC charge uses absolute code steps and dissipative switching; return-charge reuse and capacitor mismatch are unmodeled. Input acquisition uses linear endpoints; half-LSB midpoint convention is assigned. Optional asynchronous regeneration uses a snapshot input and explicit exponential law; both I/Q wait for the slower decision, DAC settling intervals are preserved, and shared reference forcing is reevaluated at actual event times. Its input snapshot, fixed launch and regeneration law are hypotheses, not physical metastability or sequencer qualification. Fixed-slot mode still assumes timely ideal-sign decisions.

load_response.scope: Local reference recharge port only, superposed with host ripple at full planning DC. Positive source charge is conserved; sink current receives no supply-energy credit. Assigned 200 ps supply-current pole requires an internal charge path; not a validated buffer. FFT guards, finite grid and linear fixed PDN do not qualify physical peak current or broadband transistor noise. Fixed reserved current is replaced by recharge; zero-recharge prehistory/tail and settled DC background are explicit assumptions. FFT response remains a finite guarded approximation. Coupled tied-return REF_IN voltage is exposed; the delivered-clock consumer must separately solve perturbed threshold events.

comparator_deadlines.scope: Assigned exponential regeneration, unity input gain and fixed launch delay; conditional deadline counts on the ideal-sign trajectory, not a metastability probability or corrected ADC simulation. Input-referred noise is already included; physical regeneration noise, supply dependence, internal kickback and recovery remain unmodeled. Any unresolved decision prevents this screen from qualifying the ideal-sign ENOB result for that comparator hypothesis.

result.scope: Known sine characterization, not protocol training. I and Q are tested together against their shared reference. Full-scale-normalized ENOB includes residual harmonic distortion and noise after fitting only a fundamental and DC. This stimulus has its own reference-current/PDN feedback; it does not borrow an OFDM load trajectory. Assigned noise, poles, midpoint-held supply sensitivity and comparator interval still need physical evidence.

internal_protection.scope: Finite ground-referenced negative clamp and explicit added capacitance on each divider node. Same50fF-equivalent charge and50ps pulses through TMDS-to-isolated change with retained external drive. Full Cartesian drop/resistance/capacitance/polarity sweep. Sampled minima and current peaks, integrated return charge; no physical diode/ESD/positive clamp/leakage/ground-bounce model. switch_charge.scope: Assigned signed charge=equivalent control coupling times3.3V, on each of four nodes at break and make. Injection work is separate from chip/peer supply work; physical control-driver power remains unallocated.

ground_referenced_protection.scope: Assigned shunt law, capacitance already in pad hypothesis. 3.6V is a diagnostic terminal screen, not a GF180 absolute maximum. No ESD trigger/holding/thermal or internal transistor terminal model.

shared_pad.scope: One retained four-node network across serial, TMDS, reset and USB. DC rail uses the wired common ledger, with a separate USB allocation when supplied. The change of supply operating point is imposed, not a regulator/PDN transient. Small-signal transfer excludes package inductance. Assigned divider and clamp values; no ESD, oxide stress or safe protection proof. Mode transitions include assigned command delay and break-before-make interval. Separate finite charge-pulse hypotheses probe injection; transistor switch edges, skew and physical slew remain open.

result.fixed_8enob_comparison_scope: Independent fixed benchmark; design acceptance uses design_enob_targets

converter.diagnostic_scope: Ratiometric internal endpoint with optional effective source charge per quarter-reference lane, lumped at acquisition end. Same finite acquisition and retained reference/DAC/comparator path. Zero effective capacitance is an ideal-load control. Continuous source impedance/bias, ratio mismatch and switch injection remain unmodeled. Cannot establish absolute VREF or independent gain accuracy.
converter.timing_ownership: Acquisition timestamps supplied by sample clock; allocated local completion intervals need no further external LO edges. Not a physical sequencer implementation.
converter.scope: Predictive conditional charge/settling/decision recurrence, not fitted silicon. Effective CDAC charge uses absolute code steps and dissipative switching; return-charge reuse and capacitor mismatch are unmodeled. Input acquisition uses linear endpoints; half-LSB midpoint convention is assigned. Optional asynchronous regeneration uses a snapshot input and explicit exponential law; both I/Q wait for the slower decision, DAC settling intervals are preserved, and shared reference forcing is reevaluated at actual event times. Its input snapshot, fixed launch and regeneration law are hypotheses, not physical metastability or sequencer qualification. Fixed-slot mode still assumes timely ideal-sign decisions.

load_response.scope: Local reference recharge port only, superposed with host ripple at full planning DC. Positive source charge is conserved; sink current receives no supply-energy credit. Assigned 200 ps supply-current pole requires an internal charge path; not a validated buffer. FFT guards, finite grid and linear fixed PDN do not qualify physical peak current or broadband transistor noise. Fixed reserved current is replaced by recharge; zero-recharge prehistory/tail and settled DC background are explicit assumptions. FFT response remains a finite guarded approximation. Coupled tied-return REF_IN voltage is exposed; the delivered-clock consumer must separately solve perturbed threshold events.

comparator_deadlines.scope: Assigned exponential regeneration, unity input gain and fixed launch delay; conditional deadline counts on the ideal-sign trajectory, not a metastability probability or corrected ADC simulation. Input-referred noise is already included; physical regeneration noise, supply dependence, internal kickback and recovery remain unmodeled. Any unresolved decision prevents this screen from qualifying the ideal-sign ENOB result for that comparator hypothesis.

result.scope: Known sine characterization, not protocol training. I and Q are tested together against their shared reference. Full-scale-normalized ENOB includes residual harmonic distortion and noise after fitting only a fundamental and DC. This stimulus has its own reference-current/PDN feedback; it does not borrow an OFDM load trajectory. Assigned noise, poles, midpoint-held supply sensitivity and comparator interval still need physical evidence.

usb_supply.scope: USB inventory ceiling through common DC network; no activity shutdown credit, no delivered USB clock or dynamic package feedback qualification.

transitions.scope: Finite command delay and isolation interval; atomic switch edges, optional finite assigned charge pulses, no transistor switch-slew or control-skew model. Pulse voltage extrema are solver-sampled, not continuous-time stress guarantees. Output drive remains released after make.

Finite command delay and isolation interval; atomic switch edges, optional finite assigned charge pulses, no transistor switch-slew or control-skew model. Pulse voltage extrema are solver-sampled, not continuous-time stress guarantees. Output drive remains released after make.

power_cycles.scope: External3.3V/50ohm sources retained through explicit isolation then finite rail fall/off/rise. Rail is forced and can absorb reverse current; this does not predict a floating or back-powered supply voltage. Recorded backfeed charge/current, sampled node extrema and energy balance; no automatic brownout-isolation delay, switch stress or missing junction proof.

internal_protection.scope: Finite ground-referenced negative clamp and explicit added capacitance on each divider node. Same50fF-equivalent charge and50ps pulses through TMDS-to-isolated change with retained external drive. Full Cartesian drop/resistance/capacitance/polarity sweep. Sampled minima and current peaks, integrated return charge; no physical diode/ESD/positive clamp/leakage/ground-bounce model. Zero-supply backfeed is a final-state topology check, not a power-collapse transient. No cost or safe stress verdict.

switch_charge.scope: Assigned signed charge=equivalent control coupling times3.3V, on each of four nodes at break and make. Finite constant-current pulses, both polarities and two widths, retained external drive. No measured switch parameters, exhaustive correlations, internal clamps, oxide-stress limits or continuous-time extrema guarantee. Injection work is separate from chip/peer supply work; physical control-driver power remains unallocated.

ground_referenced_protection.scope: Assigned shunt law, capacitance already in pad hypothesis. 3.6V is a diagnostic terminal screen, not a GF180 absolute maximum. No ESD trigger/holding/thermal or internal transistor terminal model.

shared_pad.scope: One retained four-node network across serial, TMDS, reset and USB. DC rail uses the wired common ledger, with a separate USB allocation when supplied. The change of supply operating point is imposed, not a regulator/PDN transient. Small-signal transfer excludes package inductance. Assigned divider and clamp values; no ESD, oxide stress or safe protection proof. Mode transitions include assigned command delay and break-before-make interval. Separate finite charge-pulse hypotheses probe injection; transistor switch edges, skew and physical slew remain open.

result.readiness_rule: Acquire on 64 detected transitions below0.1UI. Tracking uses latest detected error plus the larger of0.0625UI and the optional timestamp bound in UI, and gap times effective residual frequency plus integrated declared frequency slew, strictly below0.25UI and within the configured holdover count. Loss clears acquisition history. Residual-bound violations are independently reported; assigned model rule, not a protocol tolerance mask.
assumptions: Numerical voltage brackets with selectable linear interpolation or within-bracket roots; unchanged feedback and assigned 5 ps IID detector timestamp noise. Solver subdivisions are not physical phase-count requirements.

Sinusoidal or supplied multi-tone aperture displacement moves all analog observations; voltage noise plus DC offset precedes decisions. Supplied tones must guarantee monotonic time. Assigned stresses, not measured spectra.

Unchanged 512UI gap and quarter-UI acceptance limits. Window misses preserve propagated uncertainty. No source timing enters feedback. cases.detector_scope: Early/late experiment uses three voltage samples only. Gains are explicit hypotheses; no phase magnitude observer is implemented, so timing qualification must stay false even if bits decode. No timestamp oracle enters feedback.

cases.coupling_scope: Only local supply-to-aperture delay tones scaled; rail waveform, signal amplitude, detector noise and physical allocations unchanged. Each loop reruns causally. No current/area cost or physical attainment inferred.
cases.scope: Two nominal-bit-time triangular SSC cycles, identical inventory/package/channel, initial phase/offset and noise seed. measured_gap_phase.attribution_scope: Signed algebraic components at the worst recorded sample; not independent noise powers or causal intervention results.

result.readiness_rule: Unwindowed early/late mode has no phase-bound observation and never asserts qualified. Windowed early/late uses its observed phase bracket, never the true edge error; timestamp fixtures use detected magnitudes. Acquire on 64 detected transitions below0.1UI. Tracking uses latest detected error plus the larger of0.0625UI and the optional timestamp bound in UI, and gap times effective residual frequency plus integrated declared frequency slew, strictly below0.25UI and within the configured holdover count. Loss clears acquisition history. Residual-bound violations are independently reported; assigned model rule, not a protocol tolerance mask.
assumptions: Timestamp fixtures use numerical voltage brackets with interpolation or roots; early/late mode uses previous DATA, boundary and current DATA voltage samples without roots. Detector noise is the per-case assigned RMS (legacy default5ps), applied to timestamps or boundary sampling respectively. Numerical subdivisions are not physical phase-count requirements.
Fixed physical two-pole channel, 400 mV nominal differential peak with optional declared amplitude scale, zero voltage decision threshold.
Random NRZ fixture; independent held-out scoreboard interval; no source labels reach the controller.

Physical detector, stochastic noise tails, SSC, longer runs and voltage/timing variation remain open.

result.calibration_generation_scope: FPGA-side generation advances once per observed transfer fault and caught USB analog fault in this schedule. Normal STOP/reconfiguration/rearm do not renew records. Normal post-fault RF capture is raw; prior diagnostic data is rejected by the shared validity gate. No serialized fault-poll latency, fitted coefficients or measured calibration requalification.
result.diagnostic_scope: Stopped zero then +/-VREF/4 then normal selections across existing RF epochs; actual host delivery and retained reference/package. Assigned0.25pF effective reference load per selected quarter-reference lane. No inferred absolute VREF, continuous diagnostic driver model, fitted correction deployment or calibration-validity policy.

shared_supply_stress.scope: Assigned simultaneous stress, not a package-derived bound: -1% source, rail disturbance at the recorded amplitude and frequency and fourfold delay sensitivity. One analytic disturbance drives converter/gain rails and filtered LO/sample/monitor timing. Does not cover host harmonics, oscillator phase noise, cold startup or uncertain rail ownership.

reference_charge_accounting.scope: One retained reservoir across all modeled idle, SAR and TX-reference-observation intervals, including startup and fault recovery. Repeated boundary observations do not recharge twice. Native TX DAC reference draw is still unmodeled, so this is conservation of represented loads, not total reference power closure or package-current feedback.

result.analog_qualification_scope: 100 ns model observations during startup; RF RX observations at completed conversions and reference/supply observations at consumed TX words. Independent 100 ns idle observations read retained reference recovery without advancing converter state when enabled. Observation coverage expires at the declared maximum age (default 200 ns); None is an explicit held-observation control. No physical sensing implementation, between-observation voltage bound, filter/gain readiness or complete TX validity monitor.

rf_quality.scope: Four HE20 DATA symbols; first two known training, final two held out. Fixed gain, ideal frame boundary, no real preamble/CFO search/AGC or PER claim. No hidden clock or reference supplied to observer.

rf_frontend.scope: Shared antenna loss/noise/nonlinearity and package-driven gain/LO phase feed retained finite-zero filter and SAR. Selected wanted waveform, fixed gain, midpoint forcing at at least 320 MS/s; zero input during inactive intervals with natural filter decay. No packet acquisition, AGC, independent source phase noise or converter-current feedback.

host_received_iq.scope: Only complete samples reconstructed from actual 10-bit host words. Nominal FPGA timestamps exclude hidden package timing error; trailing partial sample is not padded or evaluated.

stages.payload_clock_owner: package-delayed RF RX/TX and wired TX; wired RX independent peer

host_preparation.amplitude_proof_scope: Sampled waveform check only when all-history code bound fails; continuous overshoot and unseen history remain unqualified

supply_gain_model.definition: Fractional gain response to fractional rail variation: H(s)=high_frequency_elasticity+(dc_elasticity-high_frequency_elasticity)/(1+s/(2*pi*pole_hz)). Equal unit coefficients retain the existing rail-proportional law; the pole is inactive in that baseline. Headroom always uses actual rail. Nonunit values require qualified bias/output rejection and resources; no ideal regulation assumed.

driver_parameters.topology: differential resistively loaded RF driver with programmable transconductance

correlated_supply_bound.proof: Gain-scaled open swing and each voltage/current limit are affine in the same instantaneous rail. Their difference is concave piecewise affine, so its minimum on the closed rail interval occurs at an endpoint. Assumes the existing memoryless rail/gain law and amplitude limit at all times; no transistor transient or waveform amplitude proof.

amplitude_requirement.scope: Worst supply gain versus minimum rail headroom; triangle bound on the full stable filter impulse response. Native code radius includes both I and Q jointly and must hold for all retained history. Conservative sufficient alternative, not maximum usable power or an ENOB/EVM guarantee.

electrical.scope: Conservative declared port voltage/current/energy bounds; no physical parameter validation, clipping waveform, noise or matching-network qualification

tx_rf_port.scope: Actual consumed words through retained native DAC/reconstruction and shared mixer/driver/load. Active interval only; ideal mute at STOP/fault. No physical switching tail, TX noise, DAC charge/current feedback or protocol qualification.

data_interval_power.scope: Scheduled four-symbol DATA interval at the modeled resistive load, including waveform ramp/settling; excludes idle capture padding. Not antenna power, a complete packet, emissions qualification or a minimum useful-power requirement.

spectral_diagnostic.scope: Finite DATA-window complex-envelope band-power diagnostic before observer filtering. Adjacent bands are illustrative 20 MHz bands, not standard mask/ACLR acceptance. Excludes packet switching, external RF filtering, RF harmonics and frequencies outside sampled envelope. No absolute-power estimate from windowed FFT.

result.scope: One BehavioralChip RF RX/RF TX/wired duplex/RF RX/RF TX fault/recovered RF TX/recovered RF RX sequence drives one LocalLoadTransient using one architecture current inventory and both local/HOST load inputs. Assumed warm RF operating point initially; stopped chip retains previous analog load until next configuration. Assigned 100 ns ramp, reference/supply model-observed startup and deterministic bit-checked transport with contract queue depth. Package delay shifts wired TX and RF RX/TX events. Wired RX uses independent peer timing alongside delayed local TX. Default stages STOP and rearm. The explicit turnaround variant retains the first RF stream through RX/TX/RX with assigned settling and ideal mute; no physical fast-TDD qualification follows. TX verification includes data beyond prefill. Preview uses the scheduled load without changing live state and is invalidated by epoch stop. Final RF TX and recovery share a package-delayed divide-by-64 reference-presence monitor with a prescribed 1 us source gap. Actual source-failure dynamics are not modeled. The fault stops payload, STOP discards its queue and invalidates epoch callbacks, and explicit return/rearm restores verified TX data without resetting package state. All stages arm through model-observed reference/supply validity and the existing startup guard. RF RX words now come from retained paired 10-bit SAR conversions of the selected antenna-level wanted waveform plus 12 MHz blocker through the shared noisy nonlinear frontend and retained finite-zero RX filter, packed as two 12-bit transport values. Acquisition completion follows package-delayed sample edges; words enter transport only after the allocated 18 ns decision latency. The converter reads acquisition, sampling-capacitance, diagnostic-switch loading and cycle guard from the architecture inventory and executes through the chip-owned epoch/configuration binding. Asynchronous paired decisions use the explicit50ps regeneration/100ps launch/200mV threshold hypothesis with actual reference recovery timing. Completed words publish at the unchanged18ns ceiling; early completion does not advance host events. Physical comparator/sequencer behavior remains unqualified. Reference bias stays enabled with normally 1 V upstream target (the optional USB extension explicitly disturbs it); completed SAR charge/RNG state survives TX/wired/STOP intervals and idle recovery uses retained package history at 1 us midpoint steps. ADC is parked outside RX, with idle state advanced lazily on next conversion. Startup READY now uses 100 ns model-observed reference/supply validity and the existing guard. RF RX completion observations can invalidate payload. No physical sensor or between-observation envelope is inferred. No converter-current feedback into package, physical RF block qualification, host/clock-source noise, or full RF TX port. RF TX words drive the existing native DAC and third-order reconstruction at the selected cutoff using actual consumption timestamps, retained held-code history and shared reference idle recovery. Filter state is not reset at STOP or mode change; code holds while RF output is assumed muted. Native DAC transfer is memoryless and its reference loading is not modeled; the shared mixer/driver/load transfer is evaluated, but physical output circuitry, mute waveform, spectral mask and TX current feedback remain unqualified. Not cold-start, analog settling or protocol qualification.

result.scope: One BehavioralChip RF RX/RF TX/wired duplex/RF RX/RF TX fault/recovered RF TX/recovered RF RX sequence drives one LocalLoadTransient using one architecture current inventory and both local/HOST load inputs. Assumed warm RF operating point initially; stopped chip retains previous analog load until next configuration. Assigned 100 ns ramp, reference/supply model-observed startup and deterministic bit-checked transport with contract queue depth. Package delay shifts wired TX and RF RX/TX events. Wired RX uses independent peer timing alongside delayed local TX. Default stages STOP and rearm. The explicit turnaround variant retains the first RF stream through RX/TX/RX with assigned settling and ideal mute; no physical fast-TDD qualification follows. TX verification includes data beyond prefill. Preview uses the scheduled load without changing live state and is invalidated by epoch stop. Final RF TX and recovery share a package-delayed divide-by-64 reference-presence monitor with a prescribed 1 us source gap. Actual source-failure dynamics are not modeled. The fault stops payload, STOP discards its queue and invalidates epoch callbacks, and explicit return/rearm restores verified TX data without resetting package state. All stages arm through model-observed reference/supply validity and the existing startup guard. RF RX words now come from retained paired 10-bit SAR conversions of the selected antenna-level wanted waveform plus 12 MHz blocker through the shared noisy nonlinear frontend and retained finite-zero RX filter, packed as two 12-bit transport values. Acquisition completion follows package-delayed sample edges; words enter transport only after the inventory decision latency. The converter reads acquisition, sampling-capacitance, diagnostic-switch loading and cycle guard from the architecture inventory and executes through the chip-owned epoch/configuration binding. Asynchronous paired decisions use the explicit50ps regeneration/100ps launch/200mV threshold hypothesis with actual reference recovery timing. Completed words publish at the inventory decision ceiling; early completion does not advance host events. Physical comparator/sequencer behavior remains unqualified. Reference bias stays enabled with normally 1 V upstream target (the optional USB extension explicitly disturbs it); completed SAR charge/RNG state survives TX/wired/STOP intervals and idle recovery uses retained package history at 1 us midpoint steps. ADC is parked outside RX, with idle state advanced lazily on next conversion. Startup READY now uses 100 ns model-observed reference/supply validity and the existing guard. RF RX completion observations can invalidate payload. No physical sensor or between-observation envelope is inferred. No converter-current feedback into package, physical RF block qualification, host/clock-source noise, or full RF TX port. RF TX words drive the existing native DAC and selected reconstruction at the selected cutoff using actual consumption timestamps, retained held-code history and shared reference idle recovery. Filter state is not reset at STOP or mode change; code holds while RF output is assumed muted. Native DAC transfer is memoryless and its reference loading is not modeled; the shared mixer/driver/load transfer is evaluated, but physical output circuitry, mute waveform, spectral mask and TX current feedback remain unqualified. Not cold-start, analog settling or protocol qualification.

result.scope: Selected correction and DAC ENOB with charged timing and finite queues. Seeded DATA whitening is diagnostic, not HE scrambling. Prescribed rail/phase and normalized TX remain simplified fixtures; no HE PPDU, PER, watts or emission-mask qualification.

model_assumptions.reason: Explicit loop/noise/coupling candidates, not proven selectable circuit settings

diagnostic_intervention.reason: Fixed loop/channel requirement hypotheses; not a resolved selectable chip configuration

measured_gap_phase.attribution_scope: Signed algebraic components at the worst recorded sample; not independent noise powers or causal intervention results.
measured_gap_phase.scope: Independent source-phase versus actual sample-phase drift; initial receiver phase budget including its assigned edge uncertainty. Sampled extrema, not a continuous-time or physical jitter-mask proof.

result.readiness_rule: Unwindowed early/late mode has no phase-bound observation and never asserts qualified. Windowed early/late uses its observed phase bracket, never the true edge error; timestamp fixtures use detected magnitudes. Acquire on 64 detected transitions below0.1UI. Tracking uses latest detected error plus the larger of0.0625UI and the optional timestamp bound in UI, and gap times effective residual frequency plus integrated declared frequency slew, strictly below0.25UI and within the configured holdover count. Windowed early/late uses its observed phase bracket, never the true edge error; timestamp fixtures use detected magnitudes. Acquire on 64 detected transitions below0.1UI. Tracking uses latest detected error plus the larger of0.0625UI and the optional timestamp bound in UI, and gap times effective residual frequency plus integrated declared frequency slew, strictly below0.25UI and within the configured holdover count. Loss clears acquisition history. Residual-bound violations are independently reported; assigned model rule, not a protocol tolerance mask.
assumptions: Timestamp fixtures use numerical voltage brackets with interpolation or roots; early/late mode uses previous DATA, boundary and current DATA voltage samples without roots. Detector noise is the per-case assigned RMS (legacy default5ps), applied to timestamps or boundary sampling respectively. Numerical subdivisions are not physical phase-count requirements.
Fixed physical two-pole channel, 400 mV nominal differential peak with optional declared amplitude scale, zero voltage decision threshold.
Random NRZ fixture; independent held-out scoreboard interval; no source labels reach the controller.

Sinusoidal or supplied multi-tone aperture displacement moves all analog observations; voltage noise plus DC offset precedes decisions. Supplied tones must guarantee monotonic time. Assigned stresses, not measured spectra.
unresolved: Detector timestamp noise is not transmitter or sampling-clock jitter.
Zero decision errors do not establish the 100 mV envelope threshold, BER or protocol compliance.

Optional rail-proportional gain is an assigned sensitivity. Driver placement propagates continuous forcing through channel/CTLE state; receiver placement scales the observed signal. Neither is a measured device law.
Optional CTLE is a stable unity-DC lead transfer before the assigned output noise/offset; its gain bandwidth, added noise, internal swing and current still require circuit evidence.
Physical detector, stochastic noise tails, SSC, longer runs and voltage/timing variation remain open.

operating_conditions.scope: Temperature affects frontend and sampling thermal noise only; gain, delay, phase noise, leakage and current temperature coefficients are not modeled.

clock.envelope_scope: Assigned shared incremental input envelopes. Conservative peak bounds exceeding it do not prove actual overvoltage, physical damage or loss of clock edges.

results.scope: Received local comparator bits and nominal phase slots only; no source timing enters feedback. Phase bank and optional periodic predictor are selected mathematical hardware; sampler current/loading/area and actuator implementation remain unqualified. Assigned initial coarse frequency; recorded trajectory/gaps determine scope. Cold acquisition, actuator latency, independent seeds/SSC phases and physical compatibility unqualified.
